newsitem.title: HUNGARY: INTERVIEW - Servier's presence catalyses Egis.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Servier's presence catalyses Egis.

text.p: One year after Servier S.A. acquired a 51 percent stake in Hungarian pharmaceuticals firm Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt the presence of the French partner is paying off, Egis's CEO said on Wednesday.

"Servier's presence has a catalytic impact on the company's (Egis's) operation, namely, that people believe fine tuning of details is of strategic importance," Istvan Orban, Egis's chief executive officer, told Reuters in an interview. "This is a very important perception in Hungary."
In the first year of joint work between Egis and Servier the two partners established the conditions of cooperation.
"We established the system of information technology which measures the company's performance according to the standards of the Servier group," Orban said.
The two partners also made efforts to bring Egis's planning system in harmony with that of Servier and the two companies began to plan jointly, he said.
"The most important basic of joint planning is related to market presence, namely the jointly drafted marketing plans," he said.
The other key area beside marketing where Egis had expected to benefit from Servier's presence was research and development. "In the field of development we rapidly began the joint work," Orban said.

"This means the appearance of Egis products on areas marked by Servier and also means the appearance of Servier products on Egis' markets, too. Preparations for this are under way and this means the registration procedures."

"We began to proceed on those two strategic areas (marketing and R&D) where (Egis's) operation needed improvement... and Egis started a new path of development," Orban said, adding that Egis' long-term competitiveness was perhaps the most important target for the management.
Speaking about the company's growth prospects Orban said he saw more opportunities in exports.

"We are strengthening our presence on the Hungarian market, we are increasing our network of promotional visits to doctors, but we mustn't allow that exports would be of secondary importance," Orban said. "Now exports could probably be better as the source of growth than four or five years ago."

Egis's main export markets are in central and eastern Europe where Egis has advantages over its competitors on two areas -- its already registered products have more acceptable prices than those of the competitors, while the knowledge about registrations systems in these countries gives an edge.
"What we have to take into consideration on these markets is the strengthening of market protection," Orban said.

Asked what he thinks of Egis shares as one of the best performing Hungarian stocks this year, he said: "The number one challenge for us is the implementation of the strategy. If we do it well it will have a positive impact on share prices."
